name: Jacob
title: The Patriarch of Israel
summary: Jacob, the son of Isaac and Rebekah, was the patriarch who received the name Israel after wrestling with God. He became the father of twelve sons who were the ancestors of the twelve tribes of Israel, playing a central role in the history of God's covenant.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Birth and the Right of the Firstborn
keyEvents.description: Jacob was born as a twin with Esau and held onto Esau's heel. Later, he bought the birthright from Esau for a bowl of lentil stew.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Deceives to Receive the Blessing
keyEvents.description: With help from his mother Rebekah, Jacob deceived his blind father Isaac into giving him the blessing intended for Esau, which led to conflict between the brothers.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
keyEvents.description: Fleeing from Esau, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and down, and God confirmed the covenant promises given to Abraham and Isaac.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Serves Laban for Rachel and Leah
keyEvents.description: Jacob worked fourteen years for his uncle Laban to marry Rachel, but was first tricked into marrying her older sister Leah.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Wrestles with God at Jabbok
keyEvents.description: Jacob wrestled all night with a mysterious figure by the river Jabbok and received the name Israel, which means 'he who struggles with God'.

keyEvents.title: Jacob Goes to Egypt and Meets Joseph
keyEvents.description: In his old age, Jacob traveled with his entire family to Egypt after learning that his son Joseph was alive and had become a powerful man in Egypt.
